complexity.notes: Correct but does redundant work: an O(n) solution exists via ||a single bottom-up pass where each recursive call returns its subtree's height (or -1 once an imbalance is found), so every node is visited once||. Also note `Optional` is used in annotations without being imported; under PEP 649 on CPython 3.14 annotations are never evaluated, so this is harmless, but importing it from `typing` would be tidier. The maxDepth calls also run even after a child subtree is already known to be unbalanced; evaluating the depth check first would short-circuit slightly sooner on unbalanced inputs.
complexity.summary: Top-down recursion: at each node it checks that the subtree heights differ by at most one, where each height is recomputed from scratch by a separate maxDepth traversal. Since heights are recomputed at every node, total work is proportional to n times the tree's depth.
